teach.trayEmpty: You have taught the bunny with every berry.
teach.guessHeading: New berries — the bunny has never seen these

teach.missed: The bunny got {correct} of {total} right. Teach it a berry that looks like the one it got wrong.
teach.trayHelp: The bunny ate these before, so we know what happened. Pick which ones to teach it with.
teach.guessHelp: These are the mystery berries. The bunny has to work them out from what you taught it.
teach.tryAgain: Not quite yet — teach the bunny a berry like the one it got wrong.
teach.submitFailed: Something went wrong sending that to the bunny. Try pressing Test again.
teach.walk1Body: It has no rule for which berries are safe. You are not going to write one either — there is no code in this level at all.
teach.walk2Body: Each berry here has already been eaten once, so we know what happened. Put some into the baskets. That is all 'teaching' means.
teach.walk3Body: The ? berries are ones it has never seen. To guess, it finds the berry YOU taught it that looks most like the new one, and copies that answer.
teach.walk4Body: If you only ever show it small berries, a big one will look most like the wrong thing — and it will be confidently wrong. Pick examples that cover every kind.
teach.bucketsHelp: Everything you teach it lands here. Click a berry to take it back out.
teach.tooManyExamples: That is {used} examples, and you may only use {max}. Take some back out and pick the ones that teach it the most.
teach.recapTaught: You showed it {count} berries, and nothing else:
teach.recapDecided: Then it worked out the new ones by copying whichever of yours each one looked most like:
teach.improveFewer: The bunny can be taught with as few as {max} examples. Fewer, better-chosen ones earn the last star.
teach.holdHelp: Set aside at least {min} cells the model will NOT learn from. They become your private exam.
teach.selfScore: Your model gets {right} of {total} of YOUR test right.
teach.needMoreHeldBack: Keep at least {need} cells back for testing before you press the button.
teach.safetyRule: The lab's rule: NEVER call a {danger} cell fine. Up to {allowed} careful-mistakes the other way are allowed.
teach.calledADangerousOneSafe: The robot called a {danger} cell fine. That is the one mistake the lab cannot allow — teach it more cells like the one it missed.
teach.tooManyFalseAlarms: Too many false alarms — more than {max}. Careful is good, but a robot that rejects everything is useless too.

group.runFirst: Place your flags, then press Run — the score that counts is where the machine stops.
group.boardHelp: Click an empty spot to plant a flag (up to {max}). Click a flag to pick it up.
group.nudgeHelp: Arrow keys move the chosen flag one small step.
group.meterEmpty: Plant your first flag and every dot will join the flag nearest to it.
group.meterReading: Your piles are {score}% tight. You need {need}% to win.
group.excludeReading: Strike this reading out — not an animal
group.pilesNotTight: Your piles reached {score}%, and the machine needs {need}%. Look for a flag that is holding two piles at once.
group.emptyMarker: One of your flags has no dots at all. Every flag must own at least one.
group.submitFailed: That did not go through. Nothing is wrong with your answer — try again.
group.tryAgain: Not yet — look at the board and try a change.
group.recapBody: You placed {flags} flags, and the piles came out {score}% tight — with nobody ever telling the machine what the dots were.
group.revealBanner: The piles you found were real: {names}!
group.improveFewerFlags: It can be done with {max} flags. Fewer, better-placed flags earn the last star.
group.walk1Body: A camera recorded these overnight. No one has written anything on them — there are no right answers hiding anywhere.
group.walk2Body: Plant a flag and every dot joins whichever flag is closest. That is all a group is. Move the flag, and the groups change.
group.walk3Title: The meter tells you how tight
group.walk3Body: Tight piles — everything close to its own flag — score high. A flag stuck between two piles scores low. Watch it move as you work.
group.walk4Body: Place your flags so every pile keeps to itself, then test. If the meter will not budge, maybe the problem is not your flags — look closely at the dots.

interventions.heading: Suggested next steps
interventions.caveat: Worked out from this student's attempts, hints and activity. You know them; this only knows their work.

REVIEW_CONCEPT.title: Review the idea behind this level together
REVIEW_CONCEPT.evidence: {attempts, plural, one {# attempt} other {# attempts}} on {level}, and the last three all failed.
REVIEW_CONCEPT.suggestion: Repeated failure on one level usually means the idea has not landed yet, not that they are not trying. A few minutes on the concept is likely to unblock the rest of the world.

HINT_RELIANCE.title: Check they can work without the last hint
HINT_RELIANCE.evidence: Needed the final hint tier on {levels, plural, one {# level} other {# levels}}.
HINT_RELIANCE.suggestion: Reaching the deepest hint on several levels can mean a gap earlier in the sequence. Try watching them start one level unaided to see where they stall.

PACING.title: They are getting there, slowly
PACING.evidence: About {minutes} minutes on {level}, which is planned for around {estimatedMinutes}.
PACING.suggestion: Worth a look at whether the time is thinking, re-reading, or fiddling. Slow and correct is fine; slow and lost is not.

CHECK_IN.title: Check in — they have gone quiet
CHECK_IN.evidence: No activity for {days, plural, =0 {several school days} one {# school day} other {# school days}}, while there is work outstanding.
CHECK_IN.suggestion: A short conversation usually finds the reason faster than more assignments will: a forgotten password and lost confidence look identical from here.

GET_STARTED.title: Help them start
GET_STARTED.suggestion: Sitting with them through the first level tends to be enough. Check they can sign in before assuming they chose not to.
